name: run_inspect
description: Read public current details or hypothetical next-upgrade previews relevant to your decision. Supply an area and, where supported, distinct current public references; omit refs to read the whole area. Empty refs are invalid. state, map, combat_history, and powers do not accept refs. state refreshes the observation without separate data. Invalid references reject the whole detail query and identify the invalid refs; a read that spans a changing public state fails rather than mixing observations. The result includes the current role observation when trustworthy. The permitted areas are state, map, combat_history, hand, draw, discard, exhaust, other, deck, options, rewards, shop, relics, potions, powers, and enemies; availability follows the current game state and role. combat_history covers the current battle's public card history. Use powers without refs for all relevant holders, and enemies with enemy refs for particular enemies. Upgrade previews are available for card-containing areas. This is read-only and reveals neither hidden order nor hidden values.

name: run_knowledge
description: Look up native game definitions and any configured supplementary knowledge relevant to run planning, including objects not currently owned. Use this for rules and explanations; use run_inspect for current offers, instances, or upgrade previews. Generic definitions do not override live prices, eligibility, or instance effects. This is a read-only query. The result includes the current role observation and requested knowledge in data. Use mode=catalog to discover supported categories and filter values, mode=search for concise matches, and mode=lookup for full entries. Search filters apply to base definitions, not live objects. An empty matches list means no match; missing lookup IDs are reported individually. Explicit lookups always return their text. Query pagination does not preserve a snapshot across catalog changes. This tool never advances the game. Search uses case-insensitive substring matching of whitespace-separated terms against native IDs, localized names, and base definition text; every term must match. Without spaces, a phrase is one substring. Exact ID or name matches rank first, then matches whose terms all occur in the ID or name, then text matches; ties use native ID order. Filters are not relaxed, and supplementary text does not select native matches. Search defaults to 5 results and accepts at most 20; use a larger limit for broad screening. total reports the match count; next_offset is null when no next page exists. Each search match includes the native definition ID, localized name, and complete native base description. Card matches also include confirmed base type, rarity, and cost. Search does not add private strategy text or generated summaries; use lookup for complete entries and configured supplements. Search category is optional: omit it to search all supported categories, or supply it to restrict results strictly. Each match includes its category. Card filters require category=card. Card filters use pools, types, rarities, and energy_costs. Pool, type, and rarity values come from catalog; they are not assumed to be native definition IDs. Catalog identifies each character's own card pool; this does not mean every card that character could obtain. energy_costs matches unupgraded base energy costs, using non-negative integers or "X", never current combat costs. Different dimensions combine with AND; alternatives within a dimension combine with OR. Omit a dimension to leave it unconstrained. Empty lists, duplicates, and unknown filter values are input errors, not empty matches. lookup accepts 1 to 20 distinct native IDs. entries contains found full entries in request order; missing_ids lists IDs absent from the native catalog in request order. Missing supplementary knowledge does not make a native definition missing. Catalog or enabled-extension failures are reported as failures, not missing IDs or empty supplements. A card lookup includes its complete base definition after the next upgrade, without recursively expanding further upgrades. Search still returns the base version. These encyclopedia values exclude live instance modifiers; inspect supplies actual instance values. Non-card entries have no upgrade version. A native definition that cannot upgrade is distinguished from an unavailable preview; actual read failures remain failures.

category.description: Supported category from catalog; omitted searches all categories.

text.description: Whitespace-separated, case-insensitive substring terms; all terms must match.

name: run_skill
description: Read task guidance and associated resources relevant to non-combat decisions and run planning. Request guidance when needed and reuse already available guidance while it remains applicable. Reading guidance does not select a route, execute game actions, or start another agent. The result includes the current role observation and requested guidance in data. Use mode=list to discover configured guidance and mode=read with its exact id to read it. To read an associated resource, also supply a resource key advertised by that guidance. Do not construct filesystem paths. No configured guidance yields an empty list; a load failure is an error, not an empty result. An unknown id or resource returns rejected; a real read failure returns failed. Explicit reads return the requested text even if it was read before. Guidance does not override tool contracts or authorize hidden information. List entries contain id, name, and a short description. Read returns the requested full text and advertised resource keys with short descriptions; an entry with no associated resources has an empty resource list. The list does not expand full texts or expose filesystem paths.

resource.description: Resource key advertised by this skill; never a filesystem path.

name: combat_act
description:
Submit ordered steps in battle: play_card with card and target when required; use_potion with potion and target when required; discard_potion; end_turn; select with refs; or interact with a listed special-interface operation. Direct actions are not duplicated as interact choices. This tool performs those steps; it does not delegate the battle. Prefer combining planned actions, anticipated selections, and follow-up plays when public information supports them. Use actual references, not list positions or invented IDs. Current costs and previews apply before the first step; predict later costs and effects from earlier steps, triggers, counters, and consumed bonuses.

Each step is checked against the native state when reached; an earlier step can make a later one legal. Use actual candidates and the displayed native count bounds. A mandatory single-candidate choice may be resolved automatically; include select only when it actually opens. A selection submits the complete final set of distinct candidates. A later action may reuse a card ref only if that actual card is still present and legal. If an unknown result changes your choice, submit through the revealing action and decide again; a draw need not stop a sequence whose remaining steps are appropriate for every result. For targeted actions, omit target only if required and exactly one legal target exists at execution; an explicit invalid target is not redirected. Omit target when the action does not use one.

The result reports outcome and the current role observation when trustworthy. If execution is unknown, submit no game actions until a fresh state reports control=ready; read-only queries remain available. Plan from that fresh state without replaying an uncertain submission. A role transition can stop the unexecuted tail. An optional reason briefly explains the batch using names rather than temporary references; do not provide a step-by-step reasoning transcript. This tool does not echo the reason.

card.description: Observed card instance reference; an earlier step may move this card into hand.

potion.description: Reference of the actual potion bottle in this node, not its slot or native definition ID.
Reference of the actual potion bottle in this node, not its slot or native definition ID.

action.description: Reference of a Mod-provided combat operation, including special game interfaces. It is bound to its semantic operation, not a changing menu position.

items.description: Use an exact supplied public reference, never a list index or an invented identifier.

refs.description: The complete final selection, not additions to the existing selection. Card, option, target, and bundle references are allowed when actual candidates allow them. Empty only when minimum is zero. A bundle reference selects that bundle as one option.

steps.description: Steps execute in array order. Structural validation occurs before any step; state-dependent legality is checked only when each step is reached.

reason.description: Optional short explanation of the game choice for this batch. Use object names, not temporary references; no step-by-step reasoning is needed.

name: run_act
description:
Submit ordered steps for non-combat decisions: interact with a listed reward, shop, event, rest-site, or special-interface operation; select with refs; or use_potion and discard_potion. Potion actions are not duplicated as interact choices. The tool executes these operations; it does not delegate the run. Prefer combining planned actions, anticipated selections, and follow-ups when public information supports them. Use the current operation and object references, not positions or invented IDs. Earlier steps can change resources, eligibility, options, prices, and effects.

Each step is checked against the native state when reached, so an earlier step can make a later one legal. Submit through a reveal and decide again if its unknown result would change your choice; do not queue an operation whose required reference is not yet known. Event or reward screens can close automatically after the last reward, so do not queue a skip or close unless the screen will remain open. A selection submits the complete final set of distinct candidates; follow the displayed min and max. A card ref can be reused by a later action only if that actual card is still present and legal. For targeted actions, omit target only if the action requires a target and exactly one legal target exists at execution; an explicit invalid target is not redirected. Omit it when the action does not use one.

The result reports outcome and the current role observation when trustworthy. If execution is unknown, submit no game actions until a fresh state reports control=ready; read-only queries remain available. Plan from that fresh state without replaying an uncertain submission. A role transition can stop the unexecuted tail. An optional reason briefly explains the batch using names rather than temporary references; do not provide a step-by-step reasoning transcript. This tool does not echo the reason.

Map destination interactions are not accepted here. Use run_plan and run_next for model-directed travel.

name: run_notes
description: Read or update this run's strategy notes. Keep useful plans and conclusions, not a copy of transient state already available in observations. A local edit must identify an unambiguous existing fragment and its replacement; a missing or ambiguous match leaves the notes unchanged. Use full replacement for initial notes or substantial reorganization. Updating notes does not perform a game action. The result includes the current state and the edit outcome; a read returns the requested note content in data. Use mode=read to get the full notes; replace with text to initialize, reorganize, or clear them; edit with old_text and new_text for one exact unique replacement. Empty new_text deletes the matching fragment. Missing or ambiguous old_text returns rejected and changes nothing. Successful writes return a compact confirmation, not the whole notes. If a write result is unknown, read the notes before deciding whether another edit is necessary; never blindly replay a write. Identify game objects in notes by localized name and native definition ID, adding distinguishing properties when relevant; do not include temporary action or card references.

new_text.description: Replacement text; empty deletes the uniquely matching old text.

name: run_plan
description: Replace the remaining route plan with a partial directed graph rooted at the current map node. Supply edges and a short reason. The graph may branch later but must have exactly one immediate next destination. This stage records the plan without displaying it. It does not move or resolve a pending choice. Previous ink may remain; only the latest accepted plan controls model-directed movement. Use current native reachability for special movement rather than ordinary map connections alone. Use only current-act node IDs. Every submitted edge must be reachable from the current node; self-loops and cycles are rejected. Later edges may include possible special moves even when they are not ordinary connections; their future legality is not guaranteed.

name: run_next
description: Enter the unique next destination in the active plan. Supply a short reason for continuing with that plan. The tool checks current native travel legality and does not resolve pending rewards or choices for you. If travel cannot proceed, use the returned reason and current state to decide whether to resolve the pending choice or replace the plan. Automatic progression is independent of the plan; read the actual position and remaining plan after movement. If map restoration is unconfirmed, wait for the program to confirm restoration before submitting game actions; a fresh ready observation alone does not clear that condition.
